nodes.label: Gradient
nodes.description: Linear, radial or angular grayscale ramp.

nodes.label: Checkerboard
nodes.description: Checkerboard of Color 1 and Color 2, Columns squares across and Rows down.

nodes.label: Grid
nodes.description: White grid lines on black, Columns cells across and Rows down, Thickness as a share of a cell’s shorter side so lines are as thick across as down. X Offset slides each row along by that much of a cell more than the one before it, and Y Offset each column down: 0.5 staggers alternate rows like brickwork, and a smaller one steps them into a diagonal.

nodes.label: Bricks
nodes.description: Running-bond brick pattern with mortar, bevel and per-brick tone variation.

nodes.label: Shape
nodes.description: A primitive shape as a mask, ready to use in one node. Every shape 2D SDF Shape draws, and Dome, a rounded height rather than a flat one: Circle, Ellipse, Square, Rhombus, Diamond, Parallelogram (Skew), Trapezoid (Top Width), Triangle, Isosceles Triangle, N-gon of Sides sides, Star of Points points with its hollows at Inner Radius, Hexagram, Cross, X, Heart, Egg (Point), Teardrop, Vesica (Narrowness), Crescent (Bite), Cut Disk (Kept), Pie and Arc (Sweep degrees), Tunnel, Stairs (Steps), Capsule (Top Size), Gear of Teeth teeth cut Tooth Depth into its rim, Cloverleaf, Line, Arrow, Chevron and Spiral of Turns turns. Thickness is how wide the drawn ones are. Each faces up where it has a way to face. Size is the shape across; Stretch X and Y make a circle an ellipse and a square a rectangle; Corner Rounding rounds the corners of shapes that have them; Outline keeps only a band Outline Width wide inside the edge, for rings and frames. Softness fades the edge inward, Rotation turns the shape clockwise and Centre places it. For many copies, feed it into Scatter. A shape placed across an edge comes back in at the other, so it tiles. To join shapes smoothly, cut one from another, offset, ring or repeat them, start from 2D SDF Shape instead.

nodes.label: Fractal Noise
nodes.description: Octaves of the Basis noise, each Lacunarity times the frequency and Diminish times the amplitude of the last, summed into Pivot + Amplitude × the sum — 0 to 1 about the middle at the defaults. Ridged octaves give sharp crests, Billow round lobes. Clouds, dirt, grime and every organic variation start here. One octave is plain Perlin, Simplex or Value noise. It replaces the single-octave Noise and the Perlin Noise nodes, whose graphs open as this.

nodes.label: Worley Noise
nodes.description: Worley noise with centred jitter. Channels hold the nearest one to four features: their distance, or what Style picks instead: the cell value, the cracks between cells, the second nearest feature or dots at the feature points. Cell Value at Jitter 0 is a grid of flat random squares. It replaces the Cells and Cell Noise nodes, whose graphs open as this.

nodes.label: Flake Noise
nodes.description: Metallic flakes, as in car paint: discs of random size, Coverage of the cells holding one, Scale of them across the image — the larger, the smaller the flakes. Output is 1 on every flake less up to Variation, which Variation Seed draws per flake — so the values can be reshuffled without moving a flake — and 0 between them. Normal is a tangent-space normal map of the flakes, each facing its own way up to 45° from straight out and flat between them; blend it into a surface's normal with Normal Blend, which can also weaken it. Presence is how near the surface each flake sits, for deciding where they overlap.

nodes.label: Wave Noise
nodes.description: Gabor-like wave noise: sine waves spread by Spread degrees around Angle, at Scale cycles per repeat, as Pivot + Amplitude × the waves. Wood grain, ripples and moiré.

nodes.label: Blue Noise
nodes.description: Blue noise: random values per cell with their local average removed, so points spread evenly instead of clumping. For dithering, stippling and scattering. Scale reaches the working resolution, one value per pixel, and no further: a cell smaller than a pixel would only alias.

nodes.label: Curl Noise
nodes.description: Curl of a fractal potential: a swirling, divergence-free flow field, X in red and Y in green, encoded like a normal map. Unlike two channels of Fractal Noise, the flow never gathers or spreads, so what it warps folds into swirls rather than pinching. Amplitude 1 fills the image at any number of octaves. Feed it to a warp for smoke, liquid and marble.

nodes.label: Constant
nodes.description: A constant value: a color from the picker, a float or vector whose components are unbounded, a 2 × 2, 3 × 3 or 4 × 4 matrix on a matrix wire, a boolean (stored as 0 or 1), or one of a list of named choices, which carries the index chosen. Int keeps a float, vector or matrix to whole numbers, and makes a float an integer.

nodes.label: Ramp Left-Right
nodes.description: Linear ramp from Left (U = 0) to Right (U = 1).

nodes.label: Ramp Top-Bottom
nodes.description: Linear ramp from Top (V = 1) to Bottom (V = 0).

nodes.label: Ramp 4 Corners
nodes.description: Bilinear ramp between the four corner values.

nodes.label: Split Left-Right
nodes.description: Left of U = Center is Left, right of it is Right, with an antialiased edge.

nodes.label: Split Top-Bottom
nodes.description: Below V = Center is Bottom, above it is Top, with an antialiased edge.

nodes.label: Random Float
nodes.description: A stable random value between Min and Max for each distinct In value, such as a cell or flake ID.

nodes.label: Random Color
nodes.description: A stable random RGB color for each distinct In value, with hue, saturation and brightness drawn from their ranges.

nodes.label: Blend
nodes.description: Composites the foreground over the background using a blending mode: Normal, which lays the foreground on, or one of Burn, Darken, Difference, Dodge, Divide, Exclusion, Hard Light, Hard Mix, Lighten, Linear Burn, Linear Dodge (Add), Linear Light, Linear Light Add Sub, Multiply, Negation, Overlay, Pin Light, Screen, Soft Light, Subtract and Vivid Light. The result is kept between 0 and 1. Mask decides how much of the blend lands where — black leaves the background showing, white lets the blend through — and Opacity does the same for the whole image at once. The two multiply, so a mask at half under an opacity of a half is a quarter.

nodes.label: Blur
nodes.description: Size is the kernel width in UV space (1 = the whole texture). Box and Gaussian are convolutions; Kawase is a fast, soft approximation of a large gaussian; Bilateral keeps edges sharp, blurring only across values closer than Edge Threshold; Anisotropic stretches a gaussian along Angle, narrowing it across by Anisotropy; Slope smears along the slope of the Slope input (Size is the distance in UV); Radial zooms or spins around Center (Size is the fraction of the distance, or of 180°); Median removes speckles and keeps edges; Map Driven blurs each pixel by Size × Amount.

nodes.label: Warp
nodes.description: Displaces the input, with Map saying how far each pixel moves. Directional pushes everything one way; Gradient pushes away from the map’s bright parts, as if they were raised; Vector reads the direction from the map’s own red and green, with 0.5 standing still; Radial pushes out from a centre, further the further out a pixel already is, fading to nothing half a tile away so the result still tiles; Multi-Directional warps several ways at once and brings the results back together, which churns a surface instead of smearing it one way.

nodes.label: UV Transform
nodes.description: Scales, rotates and offsets the coordinates the input is read at. Scale X and Scale Y work along the image’s own axes, so a square texture stretches into a brick or a plank; both are applied after the rotation, which keeps a turned stretch a stretch rather than a shear. Connect UV to transform coordinates of your own rather than the texture’s. Safe constrains the transform to one that rearranges texels without blending any — a quarter turn, a whole scale ratio and a whole number of texels — so a mask stays as crisp as it was.

nodes.label: Height to Normal
nodes.description: Converts a height map to a tangent-space normal map encoded in [0, 1], with +Y up the image (OpenGL). Scale multiplies the height. A DirectX map, with Y the other way, is written by choosing that convention when exporting.

nodes.label: Height to Curvature
nodes.description: Curvature from a height map, measured at Radius (in UV, so resolution-independent). Combined is 0.5 on flat areas, brighter on ridges and edges, darker in cavities; Convex and Concave isolate one side for edge wear or dirt masks.

nodes.label: Fresnel
nodes.description: Fresnel reflectance from a tangent-space normal map, viewed straight on: low where the surface faces you, rising to 1 where it turns away. Power sharpens the falloff; IOR sets how reflective it is face-on (glass, 1.52, gives 0.04).

nodes.label: Height to AO
nodes.description: Ambient occlusion from a height map: how much surrounding relief within Radius hides each point from the sky. Depth sets how tall a height of 1 stands, relative to the texture width. Tileable.

nodes.label: Normal to Height
nodes.description: Recovers the height a tangent-space normal map implies, by solving for the surface whose slope it is. A normal map records which way the surface faces and never how far it rose, so Scale sets the strength and 0.5 is the level that was flat. Tileable. A normal map records no absolute height, so a flat face bounded by a sharp wall comes back slightly domed: the face itself carries no slope to integrate, and only its edges say anything.

nodes.label: Height to Depth
nodes.description: Turns a height map into a depth map: the same surface measured down rather than up, white where it is deepest and black at its top, for parallax occlusion and other shaders that ask for depth. Normalize stretches the height to its own lowest and highest points first, so the deepest point is fully white and the highest fully black whatever range the height ran over; without it, depth is simply 1 − height.

nodes.label: Normal to Depth
nodes.description: The depth map a tangent-space normal map implies: the height Normal to Height recovers, turned into depth — white where deepest, black at the top — for parallax and other depth-reading shaders. Normalize stretches it to the full range, which is usually what you want, since a normal map records slopes and never how deep the surface went; without it, Scale sets the strength as in Normal to Height. Tileable, and with Normal to Height's one caveat: a flat face bounded by a sharp wall comes back slightly domed.

nodes.label: Normal to Curvature
nodes.description: Curvature from a tangent-space normal map, measured at Radius (in UV, so resolution-independent). Combined is 0.5 on flat areas, brighter on ridges and edges, darker in cavities; Convex and Concave isolate one side for edge wear or dirt masks. A normal map carries no scale, so Intensity sets the strength.

nodes.label: Normal to AO
nodes.description: Ambient occlusion from a tangent-space normal map: the height it implies is solved for, then each point is asked how much of the surrounding relief within Radius hides it from the sky. Depth sets how tall that relief stands. Tileable. A normal map records no absolute height, so a flat face bounded by a sharp wall comes back slightly domed: the face itself carries no slope to integrate, and only its edges say anything.

nodes.label: Bevel
nodes.description: Bevels the edge of a shape: how far each pixel lies from the edge, up to Width, as a height. Inner rises inside the shape, Outer outside it, and Both makes one ramp through the edge. Tileable.

nodes.label: Sharpen
nodes.description: Sharpens by adding back the detail a blur of Radius would remove. Threshold leaves flat areas alone, so fine noise is not amplified with the detail.

nodes.label: Emboss
nodes.description: Turns the input into relief lit from Angle: the difference across that direction, over mid grey. Grayscale, since an embossed color is neither the color nor the relief.

nodes.label: Edge Detect
nodes.description: Finds edges in the input, as a mask. Sobel is the usual choice; Prewitt weights every neighbour alike; Laplacian finds thin lines rather than slopes. Width spaces the samples, so a wider setting finds softer edges.

nodes.label: Swirl
nodes.description: Twists the input about a centre. The turn is Angle at the centre and nothing at Radius, so the swirl blends into what surrounds it; Falloff shapes how quickly it lets go.

nodes.label: Tile It
nodes.description: Repeats the input in a grid of X by Y cells, with the whole input in each one. X Offset shifts every row along by that fraction of a cell and Y Offset shifts every column, so half an offset gives the staggered arrangement of brickwork. Sampling decides what happens at the cell edges: Repeat keeps a tileable input seamless across them, a border shows its color between them.

nodes.label: Make Seamless
nodes.description: Makes an input tile, so its left edge meets its right and its top meets its bottom. Blend cross-fades the image with itself shifted half a tile, which keeps the middle of the image untouched and spends Blend Width near the edges hiding the join; it keeps the detail but softens a band around the seam. Mirror folds the image instead, which is exact and keeps every pixel sharp, but halves what is on show and makes it symmetrical. This node always wraps, since that is what being seamless means.

nodes.label: Histogram Scan
nodes.description: Cuts a mask out of a gradient: everything below Position goes to black and everything above to white, with Contrast deciding how abruptly. Slide Position to choose how much of a noise survives, and raise Contrast to harden the edge — at 1 it is a clean threshold, at 0 a ramp across the whole range. The usual first step in turning a noise into a shape.

nodes.label: Histogram Range
nodes.description: Squeezes the whole range into a band of width Range centred on Position. Nothing is thresholded away, only made shallower — which is how a height map is kept from using up all of its depth, or a mask kept from ever reaching pure black. At Range 1 and Position 0.5 it does nothing.

nodes.label: Histogram Select
nodes.description: Keeps a band and discards the rest: values near Position come out white and those far from it black. Range sets how wide the band is and Contrast how soft its sides — at 1 the band has hard edges, at 0 it falls away from the middle to nothing at the edge. Picks one layer out of a gradient, where Scan would take everything above a level.

nodes.label: Histogram Shift
nodes.description: Moves every value along by Shift and wraps it round, so what runs off white comes back from black. Nothing is squeezed and nothing is lost — the range is rotated rather than remapped — which makes it the one of these that can be undone exactly.

nodes.label: Histogram Normalize
nodes.description: Stretches the image so its darkest value lands on Low and its brightest on High, whatever they happened to be. A noise that only ever runs from 0.2 to 0.7 uses the whole range afterwards, without anyone having to find those numbers by hand — which is what makes this the one to reach for after a blur, a blend or a warp has quietly narrowed a map. Unlike the other histogram nodes it looks at the whole image, so it costs a pyramid to work out. All channels are stretched by the one mapping, taken from brightness, so a color keeps its hues rather than being pulled apart.

nodes.label: Scatter
nodes.description: Places Pattern many times over the image, each copy with its own size, angle and shade. X and Y Amount set the grid it places them on, and Copies per Cell puts more than one in each — which is how the count passes X × Y and how a scatter is pushed until it covers everything. Scale sizes a copy against its cell, and Random Scale, Random Rotation, Random Position and Random Value vary each one from its own part of the seed, so turning one up leaves the others as they were. Density thins the copies out, and a Mask thins them where it is dark — read once per copy, so a copy is wholly there or wholly gone rather than half faded. Blend decides what overlapping copies do: Max joins them, which is what a height or a mask wants; Add accumulates; Over lets later copies cover earlier ones by their alpha. Tileable: a copy running off one edge is the same copy arriving at the other.

nodes.label: Scatter Atlas
nodes.description: Scatter where each copy may be a different shape, taken from an atlas. Everything works as it does in Scatter; what is added is Atlas Columns, Atlas Rows and Atlas Count, which say how the atlas is laid out so a copy can pick a cell of it at random. Set them to match the Create Atlas that made it — a texture carries pixels, not the arrangement they were put in, so this cannot be read from the image. A cell left empty in the atlas scatters as a copy that does not appear.

nodes.label: Create Atlas
nodes.description: Lays several shapes out in a grid as one image, for Scatter Atlas to pick from — the difference between a field of identical pebbles and a field of pebbles. Slots fill the grid in reading order; Columns and Rows set its shape, and Count how many of the slots are used. A cell with no slot behind it is left empty rather than repeating the last one, which is how you ask for a copy that sometimes does not appear. Give Scatter Atlas the same Columns, Rows and Count.

nodes.label: Distance
nodes.description: Measures how far every pixel is from the nearest edge of a mask. Grow pushes the mask outwards, fading from 1 inside it to 0 at Distance away; Shrink eats it inwards from its own edge; Signed gives both at once with the edge sitting at a half, which lets a Levels afterwards slide the outline in or out without solving anything again. Threshold decides what counts as inside. Distance is the reach, as a fraction of the image. Sampling decides whether a shape against one edge is close to the opposite edge too, so a tiling mask stays tiling.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Shape
nodes.description: A primitive shape as a signed distance field: every pixel holds how far it is from the edge, in image widths, negative inside. Thirty-one shapes, from Circle, Ellipse, Box and polygons to Star, Hexagram, Heart, Egg, Vesica, Cut Disk, Tunnel, Stairs, Capsule, Gear and drawn ones such as Line, Arc, Cross, X, Arrow, Chevron and Spiral. Size is the shape across; Aspect sets how tall a box, ellipse, rhombus, isosceles triangle or tunnel is against its width; Corner Rounding rounds every corner without changing the size. Combine shapes with 2D SDF Combine, reshape them with 2D SDF Modify, Transform and Repeat, and turn the result into an image with 2D SDF to Mask. The field wraps at the image edge, so it tiles. For a plain mask in one node, use Shape under Patterns: the same shapes, with Softness, Outline and Stretch of its own.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Combine
nodes.description: Combines two signed distance fields. Union keeps everything either holds, Subtract cuts B out of A, Intersect keeps only where both are, XOR keeps where one is but not both, and Morph blends A into B by Amount. Join shapes the corner where the shapes meet: Sharp leaves it crisp, Smooth fills it with a rounded fillet and Chamfer with a straight bevel, Smoothness wide — the way two shapes melt into one. An unconnected input holds no shape.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Modify
nodes.description: Reshapes a signed distance field. Offset moves the edge out by Amount, or in when negative — growing a shape rounds its corners, shrinking it sharpens them. Onion hollows the shape into a band Thickness wide around its edge, and Rings repeats that, splitting each band in two, for rings within rings. Invert swaps inside and outside. Displace pushes the edge in and out by the Map — a noise gives rough, worn or wavy outlines — Amount at most either way, where 0.5 in the map leaves it.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Transform
nodes.description: Moves and reshapes a signed distance field about the image's middle, keeping it a distance field. Offset moves it, Rotation turns it clockwise and Scale X and Y size it. Mirror X and Y fold it across the middle, so one half is reflected onto the other — the quick way to a symmetrical shape. Elongate X and Y pull the two halves of the shape apart and fill the gap with its middle, turning a circle into a capsule and keeping its ends round. Bend curves the shape, more the further along it a point is.

nodes.label: 2D SDF Repeat
nodes.description: Repeats a signed distance field, each copy the whole input made smaller. Grid lays Columns by Rows of copies; Stagger moves every other row along by a share of a cell, half giving brickwork, and Random Rotation turns each copy by up to that many degrees either way, by Seed. Radial puts Count copies in a ring Radius from the middle, each Copy Size of the image across, and Face Outward turns each to point away from the middle — petals, spokes, a clock face. Repeat before combining, so the copies can be joined, cut and rounded together.

nodes.label: 2D SDF to Mask
nodes.description: Draws a signed distance field as a grayscale image. Fill is the shape, white inside. Stroke is a line Width wide along its edge. Bevel is a height rising from the edge to white at Width inside, ready for Height to Normal. Outer Glow fades from the edge to nothing at Width outside, and Inner Glow does the same inward. Contours draws lines every Spacing, Width thick, like the height lines of a map. Distance shows the field itself: grey at the edge, white Width inside and black Width outside. Offset moves the edge out, or in when negative, before any of them; Softness blurs the edges, which are never harder than a pixel, so they stay smooth at any resolution. Invert swaps black and white.

nodes.label: Mask to 2D SDF
nodes.description: Turns any mask into a signed distance field — how far every pixel is from the mask's edge, in image widths, negative inside — so a painted, generated or imported shape can be combined, grown, hollowed and repeated like an 2D SDF Shape. Threshold decides what counts as inside. Sampling decides whether a shape against one edge is measured from the opposite one too, as a tiling texture needs.

nodes.label: Polar Transform
nodes.description: Bends a flat image round into a disc, or flattens a disc back out. Wrap reads the input’s x as an angle and its y as a radius, so a horizontal ramp becomes a sweep round the middle and a row of bricks becomes a cobbled ring; Unwrap does the reverse, laying a disc out as a rectangle with angle running across it. The two are exact inverses, so you can unwrap, work on the result as an ordinary tiling image, and wrap it back. Repeat sends the image round more than once, and Angle turns the whole thing.

nodes.label: Height Blend
nodes.description: Blends two maps by which of them is higher, rather than by mixing them — so a layer settles into the low parts of what is under it instead of averaging with it. Wire the heights to Height A and Height B to decide the contest with maps other than the ones being blended; leave them and each map is its own height. Opacity tips the contest toward B rather than fading between them, and Transition is how sharply the two meet — zero cuts along the contour where they are level, wider feathers it. Mask decides where the layer applies at all, fading back to A where it is black — which is a different control from Opacity, that tips the contest rather than hiding its result. The Mask output carries the decision the node made, so the base color, roughness and normal of a layered material can all be blended by the same one.

nodes.label: Spline Path
nodes.description: A curve you draw, as a spline for other nodes to use. Select it to edit the curve in the 2D View: drag a point to move it, click the curve to add one, and alt-click one to take it away. Interpolation decides how the curve passes its points: Smooth runs through every one; Bézier does too, steered by two handles on each point that the 2D View shows — dragging one turns the other with it, and holding Alt breaks the pair for a corner; Quadratic is pulled towards each point without passing through it; Linear joins them with straight lines. Closed joins the last point back to the first. Wire the Spline output into Spline Render to draw it, or into any other spline node.

nodes.label: Spline Paths
nodes.description: Several curves drawn in one node, as a spline with a curve for each path — for cracks, veins or stalks drawn many at a time. Select it to edit the paths in the 2D View: click a path to work on it, then drag, add and remove its points as on Spline Path. New Path in Properties starts another, Delete Path removes the one being worked on, and Closed joins its ends. Interpolation applies to every path.

nodes.label: Spline Circle
nodes.description: A circle as a spline. Sides turns it into a regular polygon — three is a triangle, six a hexagon — and Arc takes less than the full turn, which leaves an open curve rather than a loop. Start Angle turns the shape; Centre and Radius place and size it, as fractions of the image.

nodes.label: Spline Render
nodes.description: Draws curves as strokes: its own curve, or every curve on its Spline input when one is wired. Select it to edit its own curve in the 2D View. Width sets the stroke, scaled at each point by that point’s own thickness, so a line can taper; Cap rounds or squares off the ends. The Height output gives the stroke a profile — Round like a cable, Linear like a ridge, Flat like a plateau — times each point’s height, ready for Height to Normal. Weave makes strands alternate over and under wherever they cross, as in a basket or a fabric, and Weave Depth is how far a strand dips to pass under. ID gives every curve a value of its own (per Seed), Along runs from 0 to 1 along each curve, and Distance is a field 0.5 on the stroke’s edge, reaching 1 and 0 at Distance Range inside and out. Tile brings a curve that runs off one edge back in at the other.

nodes.label: Spline Fill
nodes.description: Fills the inside of curves as a mask: its own curve, or every curve on its Spline input. An open curve is filled as though a straight line joined its ends. Rule decides what counts as inside where curves overlap: Non-zero fills everywhere they wind round, Even-odd fills every other layer, so a curve inside another cuts a hole in it. Tile lets a shape crossing an edge fill on both sides of it.

nodes.label: Spline Mapper
nodes.description: Lays an image along curves as a ribbon: its x runs along the curve and its y across it, so a strip of bricks follows a path and a rope winds round a loop. Width is the ribbon, scaled at each point by its thickness. Stretch fits one copy of the image to the whole curve; Repeat lays copies Tile Length × Width long, so a square image stays square however long the curve. Corners: Mitre turns the image round a corner as a picture frame’s moulding does, squeezed inside and stretched outside; Round has each pixel take the nearest point of the curve, which fans the image round the outside of a corner. Connect a Start or End image for pieces of their own at the ends of an open curve, Piece Length × Width long — frayed ends on a rope, posts at the ends of a fence — and the middle repeats a whole number of times between them so it meets both cleanly. Slide moves the middle along the curve, Flip turns the image over across it. The UV output is where each pixel read its image, for UV Transform to lay something else the same way; Mask is the ribbon itself.

nodes.label: Spline Flow
nodes.description: Draws a flow map along curves: a direction in red and green, with 0.5 meaning still — feed it to Warp in Vector mode to stream an image along a path. Along points the way each curve is heading; Outward points away from the curve on either side, to push things off it. Intensity is the strength on the curve, fading to nothing at Width/2 away; Falloff shapes the fade, from 0 (full strength to the edge) up. Reverse turns every direction round.

nodes.label: Spline Transform
nodes.description: Moves, turns and scales every curve on its Spline input about a pivot. Scale X and Scale Y stretch along the image’s own axes before the turn, so a stretched curve stays stretched when turned; Rotation turns clockwise. Scale Thickness carries the scale over to the stroke, so a curve shrunk to half is drawn half as thick.

nodes.label: Spline Warp
nodes.description: Moves every point of the curves on its Spline input by a map read where the point is. Intensity pushes each point out along the curve’s normal by the map’s brightness — black leaves it where it is, and Two Sided makes mid-grey the still point so dark pulls one way and light the other. Vector moves it by the map’s red and green, 0.5 being still, as Warp and Spline Flow read them. Amount is how far, as a fraction of the image.

nodes.label: Spline Sample
nodes.description: Sets what each point of the curves carries from a map read where the point is. Height is what Spline Render’s Height output stands the curve up by; Thickness is what scales its stroke there. Copy replaces the value with the map’s, Add and Subtract change it by the map’s, Multiply scales it by the map’s. Amount scales the map first. A thickness never goes below zero.

nodes.label: Spline Profile
nodes.description: Sets the thickness and height of every curve on its Spline input along its length, from two gradients whose left end is each curve’s start and right end its finish: white is full, black is nothing. Use it to taper, bulge or pinch a stroke, or to make a ridge rise along its length, however many points the curve has. Multiply scales what each point already carries; Replace sets it outright.

nodes.label: Spline Trace
nodes.description: Traces the outlines of a mask into curves: every edge where the mask crosses Threshold becomes a closed curve, holes included, running the opposite way round so Spline Fill leaves them empty. Flood Fill cells become stone outlines to bevel with Spline Render; a painted crack becomes a curve to warp or wiggle. Detail is how finely the mask is read — finer follows smaller shapes and costs more — and Smallest leaves out outlines of fewer steps than that, the specks of a noisy mask. With Tile on, an outline that runs off one edge continues from the other. At most 256 outlines.

nodes.label: Spline Text Outline
nodes.description: Sets text as the Text node does and gives back the outline of every letter as a curve, the counters of a, e and o included, for engraved, outlined or bevelled lettering: stroke it with Spline Render, fill it with Spline Fill, or offset it into a rim with Spline Offset. The letters are set by the browser and traced, so Detail is how closely the outline follows them — 256 keeps the corners of a large word crisp. Each letter outline is one curve; at most 256 in all.

nodes.label: Spline Trim
nodes.description: Cuts every curve on its Spline input down to the stretch between Start and End, as fractions of its length. Offset slides that stretch along the curve, and round and round a closed one. Raise End from 0 to 1 and a stroke draws itself along its curve, which is how a mask grows along a path. A cut curve is open; a stretch of no length draws nothing.

nodes.label: Spline Resample
nodes.description: Lays the vertices of every curve on its Spline input out again, evenly along its length: Count of them on every curve, or one every Spacing, so a long curve gets more. More than a curve had keeps its shape and makes it finer for Spline Warp or Spline Wiggle to bend; fewer cuts its corners, for a low-poly look. A closed curve stays closed.

nodes.label: Spline Wiggle
nodes.description: Gives every curve on its Spline input a hand-drawn wobble: each is laid out again finely and pushed to either side by a smooth noise of how far along it is. Amount is how far, Wavelength how long one wave is along the curve, and Octaves adds finer wobble on top. Because it is measured along the curve, the wobble keeps its pace on a long curve and a short one alike, and round a closed curve it comes back to where it started. Each curve wobbles its own way; change Seed for another.

nodes.label: Spline Offset
nodes.description: Moves every curve on its Spline input out to its side by Offset, keeping the same distance all along it — corners stay sharp. A closed curve grows for a positive Offset and shrinks for a negative one, whichever way it was drawn; an open one moves below a curve drawn left to right. Copies makes more, each Spacing further out, for parallel lines, rings or contour lines from one curve.

nodes.label: Spline Simplify
nodes.description: Holds every curve on its Spline input with fewer vertices, dropping each one the curve can do without while staying within Tolerance of where it was. A smooth curve of many small steps comes down to a few; raise Tolerance and it becomes a hand-cut, low-poly line. The first and last vertices always stay, and a closed curve stays closed.

nodes.label: Spline Hang
nodes.description: Hangs a cable between the points of a curve: every span from one point to the next sags into the curve a chain makes under its own weight, by Slack times its length, so a long span sags further than a short one. Angle turns which way is down, clockwise; a negative Slack bows the spans up. Draw the pegs on its own curve, or give it curves on its Spline input, whose every vertex is a peg — a Linear path, or Spline Resample to space them out. Thickness and height run evenly from peg to peg.

nodes.label: Spline Growth
nodes.description: Grows branching curves from seeds, for cracks, roots, veins, coral and lightning. Trunks start from places scattered over the image, or all from one Point, heading Direction (clockwise from pointing right) give or take Spread. Each walks Segments steps along its Length, turning by up to Jitter at every step. Every curve sprouts Branches children, down to Depth generations; a child leaves from along its parent’s middle at Branch Angle, alternating sides, and is Branch Length times as long. Taper thins each curve towards its tip, and a child starts as thick as its parent was there, so the tree thins towards its ends — the thickness also becomes each point’s height, so a crack is deepest at its trunk. At most 256 curves.

nodes.label: Spline Flow Lines
nodes.description: Draws curves that follow a map, for wood grain, water streaks, hair and currents. Count lines start on a grid over the image, each nudged by Jitter, and walk Steps steps of Step Length the way the map points where they are. Vector reads the map’s red and green, 0.5 being still, as Warp’s Vector mode and Spline Flow make it — a still place stops a line; Angle reads its brightness as a heading, 0 pointing right and 0.25 down. Feed it a blurred noise for grain, or a Spline Flow for lines that run alongside other curves. Taper thins both ends to nothing. At most 256 lines.

nodes.label: Spline Append
nodes.description: Puts the curves of up to four inputs into one list: those on A, then B, then C, then D, each unchanged. Use it to draw, fill or scatter along several curves with one node — a fill of two curves under Even-odd makes a ring.

nodes.label: Spline Merge
nodes.description: Joins every curve on its Spline input into one, in order: each runs on from the end of the one before, crossing the gap in a straight line. Closed joins the end of the last back to the start of the first. A curve can hold only so many points, so a very long join is thinned evenly along its length.

nodes.label: Spline Select
nodes.description: Keeps some of the curves on its Spline input, by their place in the list, which starts at 0. Range keeps Count of them from Start; Every keeps every Step-th from Start; Random keeps each with a chance of Probability, a different set for each Seed. Invert keeps the rest instead.

nodes.label: Spline Bridge
nodes.description: Runs Count strands between curves, each from the same place along every curve it joins. Between runs them from the last curve on A to the last curve on B, like the rungs between two rails; Through runs them through every curve on A in turn, first to last. Smooth curves the strands — between two curves each leaves square to them, through a list it passes smoothly through every curve — and Detail is how finely each curved stretch is walked. The strands are a spline like any other, and Spline Bridge Mapper lays an image across them.

nodes.label: Spline Bridge Mapper
nodes.description: Stretches an image across the strands on its Spline input — wire in Spline Bridge — so it fills the space between the curves the bridge was built on and bends with them. The image’s x runs from the first strand to the last, its y along each strand; Flip turns it over along the strands. The UV output is where each pixel read the image, for UV Transform to lay something else the same way; Mask is the area the strands cover.

nodes.label: Scatter Splines on Splines
nodes.description: Places copies of the curves on Shape along the curves on Path: Count copies along each path curve, spaced evenly by distance. Draw the shape around the middle of the image — that is the point placed on the path. With several shape curves each copy takes one at random. Scale, Rotation and their Random amounts vary the copies, Follow Curve turns each to the way the path heads, Offset slides them off it to one side, and Scale Thickness scales each copy’s stroke with it. The copies are a spline, so they can be drawn, filled, warped or scattered along in turn.

nodes.label: Spline Text
nodes.description: Sets a string along a curve — its own, or every curve on its Spline input — each character turned to the curve where it sits. Select it to drag its own curve in the 2D View. Along slides the string from one end to the other, Across lifts it off the curve so it can sit above or below the line, and Flip reads the curve backwards for text that would otherwise be upside down. The glyphs are drawn at the resolution the pass renders at, so they stay crisp at any size.

nodes.label: Spline Scatter
nodes.description: Places copies of a shape along a curve — its own, or every curve on its Spline input — evenly spaced by distance so they stay even through a bend. Select it to drag its own curve in the 2D View. Count is copies along each curve, up to 16384 over every curve together. Follow Curve turns each copy to the direction the curve is heading there; Offset slides them off the curve, to one side or the other. Closed spreads them the whole way round a loop without doubling up at the join. Copies that run off an edge arrive at the other, so the result tiles.

nodes.label: Spline Scatter Atlas
nodes.description: Places copies along curves — its own, or every curve on its Spline input — where each copy may be a different shape, taken from an atlas. Everything works as it does in Spline Scatter; what is added is Atlas Columns, Atlas Rows and Atlas Count, which say how the atlas is laid out so a copy can pick a cell of it at random. Set them to match the Create Atlas that made it — a texture carries pixels, not the arrangement they were put in, so this cannot be read from the image. A cell left empty in the atlas scatters as a copy that does not appear.

nodes.label: Kuwahara
nodes.description: Smooths an image without crossing its edges, which leaves it looking painted. Every other blur asks what the neighbourhood averages to; this asks which part of it is most uniform and answers with that part’s average — so a flat area flattens further while an edge survives, because the part lying along one side of it is far more uniform than any part straddling it. Classic uses four overlapping quadrants, which is the original and the cheapest, and shows as blockiness on anything curved. Generalized cuts a disc into Sectors and weighs each by how uniform it is rather than letting one win outright, which is smooth where Classic steps; Sharpness decides how strongly uniformity is preferred. Anisotropic first asks the image which way it is changing and squashes the disc into an ellipse lying along each edge, so the sectors follow a curve the way a brush does; Anisotropy sets how far an ellipse may stretch — at 0 it is Generalized, and even turned up a flat area stays round, having no direction to stretch along. It costs three passes more than the others. Cost grows with the square of Radius. Tileable.

nodes.label: Crop
nodes.description: Takes a rectangle of the input, given by its Left, Right, Top and Bottom edges. Stretch fills the output with it, so cropping is also zooming in; Keep leaves the rectangle its own size and in its own place and clears everything else, which makes the node a rectangular mask instead. Rotation turns the rectangle about its own centre, so a crop can follow something that is not square to the image. Dragging an edge past its opposite narrows the rectangle rather than turning it inside out.

nodes.label: Auto Crop
nodes.description: Finds the rectangle the content actually occupies and crops to it, without anyone having to measure it. Threshold decides what counts as content, and Measure chooses whether that is how bright a pixel is or how opaque — an image placed on nothing carries its shape in alpha rather than in its color. Padding leaves a margin, so a shape does not end up touching the edge of its own image. Stretch fills the output with the rectangle; Keep leaves it where it is and clears the rest. An image with nothing above the threshold has no rectangle to crop to and is handed back as it came.

nodes.label: Height to Shadow
nodes.description: The shadow a height map casts on itself from a single light. A ray is walked towards the light from every point, climbing at the light’s Elevation, and anything standing above it shuts the light out. Angle turns the light around the surface and Elevation raises it: low light throws long shadows, overhead light almost none. Depth sets how tall the relief stands, Distance how far a shadow may reach, and Softness how quickly its edge gives way. Unlike ambient occlusion this has a direction to it — a pit is dark in both, but only here does the dark sit to one side. Tileable.

nodes.label: Height to Bent Normal
nodes.description: The direction each point is most open to the sky in, from a height map. A normal map says which way a surface faces; in a groove that may be straight up while everything above it is wall, and what light arrives comes from along the groove instead. Lighting a cavity with this is what stops it reading as a flat surface with a dark patch painted on. Radius sets how far the search looks and Depth how tall the relief stands. Tileable.

nodes.label: Normal UV Transform
nodes.description: Scales, rotates and offsets the coordinates a normal map is read at, turning the stored vectors by the same angle so the relief stays lit from the direction it now faces. Use this rather than UV Transform whenever what is being moved is a normal map. Scale X and Scale Y work along the image’s own axes, as they do there: a plain transform moves the picture and leaves the vectors pointing the old way. Connect UV to transform coordinates of your own rather than the texture’s. Safe constrains the transform the way it does on UV Transform — a quarter turn, a whole scale ratio and a whole number of texels — which matters more here: the vectors are then turned by that same quarter, so every normal that comes out is one that went in.

nodes.label: Normal Blend
nodes.description: Combines two normal maps, putting Detail on top of Base. Adding them channel by channel is wrong in a way that looks almost right — the sum of two unit vectors is not one — so pick a mode instead. Reoriented turns the detail into the base’s frame, so a bump on a slope leans with the slope; it is the most correct and the one to reach for. Whiteout is cheaper and keeps detail crisp, flattening a steep base a little. Slopes adds the two surfaces’ slopes, which is what combining their heights would have done. Replace keeps only the detail. Strength leans the detail before it is combined, so turning it down leaves the base as it was rather than fading everything towards flat.

nodes.label: Normal Normalize
nodes.description: Puts every vector in a normal map back to one unit long. Anything that treats a normal map as a picture — a blur, a resize, a lossy file — leaves vectors that are no longer unit length, and a shader lighting those gets the strength of the relief wrong rather than obviously broken. Rebuild Z throws the stored blue away and works it out from red and green, which is what makes a two-channel normal map whole again. Strength leans the vectors further from or closer to straight up, which is the part that carries the relief.

nodes.label: Skew
nodes.description: Leans the image over: Horizontal slides each row sideways by how far down it is, Vertical slides each column up or down by how far across it is. The slide is measured from Center, so that line stays put and the image leans about it rather than drifting off. Amount is in whole UV, so 1 slides the far edge a whole repeat — which for a tileable image is no slide at all, and is why whole amounts keep it tiling.

nodes.label: Mirror
nodes.description: Folds the image about a line, replacing everything past it with its reflection. Position sets where the fold is, and Flip chooses which side is kept. Both folds along each axis in turn, giving four of the same quarter. Folding makes the two edges of an axis meet whatever was there before, so this is also the blunt way to make an image tile — at the cost of showing half of it twice, and of a crease down the fold.

nodes.label: Normal to Bent Normal
nodes.description: The direction each point is most open to the sky in, from a tangent-space normal map: the height it implies is solved for, then each point is asked which way the relief within Radius still leaves open. Depth sets how tall that relief stands. Tileable. A normal map records no absolute height, so a flat face bounded by a sharp wall comes back slightly domed: the face itself carries no slope to integrate, and only its edges say anything.

nodes.label: Flood Fill
nodes.description: Finds the separate shapes in a mask — runs of lit pixels that touch — and gives each one an identity of its own. Blue is a value per shape, the same everywhere within it and unrelated to its neighbours, which is what drives a color, a roughness or a height per shape. Red and green hold the shape’s identity, equal for two pixels exactly when they are in the same shape. Alpha is 1 inside a shape. Threshold sets what counts as lit, Diagonals decides whether shapes meeting only at a corner are one shape or two, Sampling decides whether a shape touching one edge continues on the other, and Quality is there for the rare mask whose shapes wind so far that the settling needs longer — if a shape comes back as two values, raise it.

nodes.label: Flood Fill to Random Grayscale
nodes.description: Gives every shape found by Flood Fill a grey of its own, the same everywhere in that shape and unrelated to its neighbours’. The usual way to vary a height, a roughness or a mask per shape rather than per pixel. Seed deals a different set of values without changing which shapes there are.

nodes.label: Flood Fill to Random Color
nodes.description: Gives every shape found by Flood Fill a color of its own. Mostly for seeing the shapes — a field of them in flat colors shows at a glance which are separate and which have been joined. Saturation pulls the colors towards grey, for tinting rather than confetti.

nodes.label: Flood Fill to Index
nodes.description: Where each shape falls in reading order — down the rows first, then along them — as a value from 0 at the top-left-most shape towards 1 at the bottom-right-most. Measured against the image rather than against the number of shapes, so it is an order and not a count: adding a shape does not renumber the others, and the values are not evenly spaced.

nodes.label: Flood Fill to Position
nodes.description: Where each pixel sits inside its own shape’s box: red runs 0 to 1 across the shape and green down it. The coordinates to read something per shape with — feed them to a UV Transform, or use them to place a gradient or a pattern inside every shape at once.

nodes.label: Flood Fill to BBox Size
nodes.description: How big each shape’s box is, as a fraction of the image: red is its width, green its height and blue the larger of the two. Fills each shape with its own size, so a mask can pick out the large shapes from the small ones.

nodes.label: Flood Fill to Gradient
nodes.description: A ramp across every shape at once, running 0 to 1 over each shape’s own box at the given Angle. Random Angle turns each shape’s ramp by its own amount, so a field of them does not read as one ramp cut into pieces.

nodes.label: Flood Fill Mapper
nodes.description: Puts a copy of Image into every shape found by Flood Fill, fitted to that shape’s own box — so one authored detail fills a field of shapes of different sizes. Scale grows or shrinks each copy from the middle of its shape, and Random Rotation turns each one a quarter at a time by its own shape, so the field does not read as the same picture stamped over and over. Anything outside a copy is left empty rather than smeared.

nodes.label: Flood Fill to Color
nodes.description: Fills every shape found by Flood Fill with the single color or value that Image holds at the middle of that shape. One reading per shape rather than per pixel, so each shape comes out flat and the pattern across them is the image’s — which is how a field of shapes takes its colors from a gradient, a photograph or a noise.

nodes.label: FXAA
nodes.description: Smooths stepped edges by blurring along each edge rather than across it, so lines lose their stair steps while flat areas and fine texture stay as they are. Threshold is how much of a step counts as an edge; Span is how far the smoothing may reach.

nodes.label: Denoise
nodes.description: Removes noise by averaging each pixel with the ones whose surroundings look like its own, rather than with whatever happens to be next to it. Detail that repeats survives where a blur would take it. Strength is how different two surroundings may be and still count; Radius is how far to look.

nodes.label: Levels
nodes.description: Remaps the input range with gamma, clipping and output range control.

nodes.label: Replace Color
nodes.description: Replaces colors within Tolerance of From with To. Softness widens the edge of the selection, and Keep Shading moves the color rather than flattening it, so highlights and shadows survive.

nodes.label: Gradient Map
nodes.description: Colorizes a grayscale input through a gradient: black takes the color at the left end, white the right. Add as many stops as you need, each with its own opacity, blended linearly, smoothly, as constant bands or along a spline.

nodes.label: HSL
nodes.description: Shifts hue and scales saturation and lightness.

nodes.label: Dither
nodes.description: Ordered dithering: every pixel gets a threshold from a Bayer matrix, so a few levels can stand for many by mixing them. Levels cuts each channel to Levels steps from 0 to 1, a pixel taking the step above where its threshold says so — a flat 50 % grey at two levels is every other pixel white — for a pixel-art or print look without the bands Color Bands leaves. Subtract Threshold gives In minus the threshold, alpha included, ready for an Alpha Clip or a Step to turn into a stippled fade. Pattern is the matrix; Cell Size makes each of its cells that many pixels across. The pattern repeats every 2, 4 or 8 cells, so at the usual power-of-two sizes it tiles.

nodes.label: Temperature
nodes.description: Tints the image by the color of a light burning at Kelvin: warm below 6500 K, cool above, neutral at it. Brightness is held, so this shifts color without changing exposure. To take a cast out rather than put one in, use White Balance.

nodes.label: White Balance
nodes.description: Moves what counts as white, the way a camera does. Temperature runs cool to warm and Tint green to magenta, correcting a cast rather than adding one. The adaptation is done in LMS, so neutrals move and saturated colors are left much as they were.

nodes.label: Contrast
nodes.description: Scales values around Pivot with Amount as a linear slope: above 1 increases contrast, between 0 and 1 reduces it.

nodes.label: Remap
nodes.description: Linearly maps values from [In Low, In High] to [Out Low, Out High].

nodes.label: Range
nodes.description: Remaps [In Low, In High] to [Out Low, Out High] with a gamma correction in between; optionally clamps to the output range.

nodes.label: Luminance
nodes.description: Luminance of the color, weighted by the luma coefficients (Rec.709 by default).

nodes.label: Colorspace Conversion
nodes.description: Converts a color from one space to another: RGB (sRGB-encoded, as a picture is stored), Linear (the light it stands for) or HSV (hue, saturation and value, each 0 to 1). HSV is reached from and left through RGB. The same space on both sides changes nothing; alpha is unchanged. It replaces the RGB to HSV and HSV to RGB nodes, which open as this.

nodes.label: HSV Adjust
nodes.description: Adds Hue Offset to the hue (1 is a full turn, wrapping), and multiplies saturation and value.

nodes.label: Color Correct
nodes.description: Hue, saturation, gamma, lift, gain, contrast and exposure in one node, applied in that order.

nodes.label: Color Bands
nodes.description: Flattens an image into bands: each channel quantised to Levels evenly spaced steps, the lowest at 0 and the highest at 1, so two levels give black and white and more give flat bands. Values are taken between 0 and 1 first. To snap numbers of any size to a grid instead, use Posterize under Math › Advanced.

nodes.label: Extract
nodes.description: One channel of the input, by index. An index past the channels the input carries is an error.

nodes.label: Convert
nodes.description: Converts to another type: a single value fills every channel; fewer channels are padded with 0 (alpha 1); more are truncated. Int truncates a float or a vector toward zero, and makes a float an integer; Boolean is true for any non-zero value.

nodes.label: Combine 2
nodes.description: Joins two streams into one: two floats, a color or vector 3 plus a float, or two vector 2s.

nodes.label: Combine 3
nodes.description: Three floats as the channels of a color or vector 3.

nodes.label: Combine 4
nodes.description: Four floats as the channels of a color or vector 4.

nodes.label: Separate 2
nodes.description: The X and Y channels of a vector 2 as floats.

nodes.label: Separate 3
nodes.description: The R, G and B (X, Y, Z) channels of a color or vector 3 as floats.

nodes.label: Separate 4
nodes.description: The R, G, B and A (X, Y, Z, W) channels of a color or vector 4 as floats.

nodes.label: If Greater
nodes.description: In 1 where Value 1 > Value 2, otherwise In 2.

nodes.label: If Greater or Equal
nodes.description: In 1 where Value 1 ≥ Value 2, otherwise In 2.

nodes.label: If Equal
nodes.description: In 1 where Value 1 = Value 2 exactly, otherwise In 2.

nodes.label: Switch
nodes.description: Outputs input floor(Which) + 1, clamped to In 1–In 10. Unconnected inputs are zero.

nodes.label: Texture
nodes.description: Uses an imported image. Linear-light color images (EXR, HDR) are converted to sRGB; choose Non-color data for normal, roughness or height maps.

nodes.label: Text
nodes.description: Sets a string into the texture, in an imported font or a generic one. Select it to place the text by hand in the 2D View. Expose any of its settings to wire a material’s input to it — a Text, a Font, a Float for the size, a Color — so whoever uses the material sets it in the Viewer.

nodes.label: SVG
nodes.description: Draws an imported SVG, rasterised at the resolution being rendered so it stays sharp at any size. Select it to place the drawing by hand in the 2D View. The Spline output is the drawing as curves — every path, rectangle, circle and line, its curves kept exactly — lying where the image draws it, ready to stroke with Spline Render, fill with Spline Fill, or bend, trim and scatter along like any curve. A path longer than a curve holds comes through as several, and at most 256 curves in all. Expose any of its settings to wire a material’s input to it — an SVG for the drawing, a Float for the scale, a Color for the tint — so whoever uses the material sets it in the Viewer.

nodes.label: UV
nodes.description: The texture's coordinates: U in red and V in green, V up. Bend them and read them back with a UV Transform.

nodes.label: IOR
nodes.description: The index of refraction of a common material: air 1.0, water 1.333, glass 1.52, diamond 2.417 and the rest. Feed it to Fresnel, or use it as the number it is; for any other value, a Constant is the node.

nodes.label: Add
nodes.description: A + B, per channel.

nodes.label: Subtract
nodes.description: A − B, per channel.

nodes.label: Multiply
nodes.description: A × B, per channel.

nodes.label: Divide
nodes.description: A ÷ B, per channel. Division by zero gives 0.

nodes.label: Modulo
nodes.description: A mod B with floored division (always the sign of B). Modulo zero gives 0.

nodes.label: Fraction
nodes.description: The fractional part of A: A − floor(A).

nodes.label: One Minus
nodes.description: 1 − A, per channel.

nodes.label: Absolute
nodes.description: Absolute value of A.

nodes.label: Sign
nodes.description: −1, 0 or 1 depending on the sign of A.

nodes.label: Floor
nodes.description: A rounded down.

nodes.label: Ceiling
nodes.description: A rounded up.

nodes.label: Round
nodes.description: A rounded to the nearest integer (halves to even).

nodes.label: Power
nodes.description: A raised to B. Undefined for negative A; see Safe Power.

nodes.label: Safe Power
nodes.description: |A| raised to B, keeping the sign of A.

nodes.label: Sine
nodes.description: Sine of A (radians).

nodes.label: Cosine
nodes.description: Cosine of A (radians).

nodes.label: Tangent
nodes.description: Tangent of A (radians).

nodes.label: Arcsine
nodes.description: Arcsine of A, clamped to [−1, 1].

nodes.label: Arccosine
nodes.description: Arccosine of A, clamped to [−1, 1].

nodes.label: Arctangent2
nodes.description: Angle of the vector (B, A): atan2(A, B), in radians.

nodes.label: Square Root
nodes.description: Square root of A; negative values read as 0.

nodes.label: Log
nodes.description: Logarithm of A to the base chosen: e, 2 or 10. Values at or below 0 read as a tiny positive number.

nodes.label: Exponential
nodes.description: The base chosen, e or 2, raised to A.

nodes.label: Clamp
nodes.description: A limited to [Min, Max].

nodes.label: Triangle Wave
nodes.description: Triangle wave of period 1: 0 at whole numbers, 1 halfway between.

nodes.label: Minimum
nodes.description: Smaller of A and B, per channel.

nodes.label: Maximum
nodes.description: Larger of A and B, per channel.

nodes.label: Distance
nodes.description: Euclidean distance between A and B, over the channels the inputs carry.

nodes.label: Dot Product
nodes.description: Dot product of A and B, over the channels the inputs carry.

nodes.label: Cross Product
nodes.description: Cross product of A and B as 3-vectors.

nodes.label: Reflection
nodes.description: Reflects A about the normal B (B should be normalized).

nodes.label: Refract
nodes.description: Refracts A through the normal B with the given ratio of indices (A and B normalized).

nodes.label: Normalize
nodes.description: A scaled to unit length, over the channels it carries. A zero vector stays zero.

nodes.label: Length
nodes.description: Length of A, over the channels it carries.

nodes.label: Smoothstep
nodes.description: HLSL smoothstep(Min, Max, A): Hermite interpolation of A between Min and Max, clamped to [0, 1]. Min above Max inverts the curve; equal bounds give a hard step.

nodes.label: Saturate
nodes.description: HLSL saturate: A clamped to [0, 1].

nodes.label: Lerp
nodes.description: Linear interpolation from A to B by T, per channel.

nodes.label: Slerp
nodes.description: Spherical interpolation from A to B by T, over the channels they carry; falls back to Lerp for parallel vectors.

nodes.label: Step
nodes.description: HLSL step(Edge, A): 0 below Edge, 1 at or above it. A hard threshold, where Smoothstep is a soft one.

nodes.label: Negate
nodes.description: −A, per channel.

nodes.label: Reciprocal
nodes.description: 1 ÷ A, per channel. The reciprocal of zero gives 0.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Square Root
nodes.description: 1 ÷ √A, per channel. Zero and negative values give 0.

nodes.label: Posterize
nodes.description: In snapped down to a grid of 1 ÷ Steps: floor(In × Steps) ÷ Steps, per channel, at any size and below zero too. Zero steps give 0. To flatten a picture into bands from black to white instead, use Color Bands under Adjustments.

nodes.label: Inverse Lerp
nodes.description: Where T lies between A and B: (T − A) ÷ (B − A), so 0 at A and 1 at B — the factor Lerp would need to give T. Equal A and B give 0.

nodes.label: Truncate
nodes.description: A with its fractional part dropped: rounded toward zero.

nodes.label: Arctangent
nodes.description: Arctangent of A, in radians.

nodes.label: Degrees To Radians
nodes.description: A in degrees, as radians: A × π ÷ 180.

nodes.label: Radians To Degrees
nodes.description: A in radians, as degrees: A × 180 ÷ π.

nodes.label: Hyperbolic Cosine
nodes.description: Hyperbolic cosine of A.

nodes.label: Hyperbolic Sine
nodes.description: Hyperbolic sine of A.

nodes.label: Hyperbolic Tangent
nodes.description: Hyperbolic tangent of A.

nodes.label: Projection
nodes.description: A projected onto B: the part of A that runs along B, over the channels the inputs carry. A zero B gives 0.

nodes.label: Rejection
nodes.description: A less its projection onto B: the part of A at right angles to B, over the channels the inputs carry.

nodes.label: Remap
nodes.description: In carried from one range to another: In Min goes to Out Min and In Max to Out Max, in a straight line and unclamped. Equal In Min and In Max give Out Min.

nodes.label: Matrix Compose
nodes.description: Builds a matrix from a move, a turn and a scale, applied scale first, then turn, then move. Rotate and Scale makes a 2 × 2 that turns and stretches a 2D vector; 2D Transform a 3 × 3 that moves one too, as a UV is moved; 3D Transform a 4 × 4 that does all three to a 3D point, turning about X, then Y, then Z. A positive 2D rotation turns clockwise on the image. Wire it into Matrix Transform to apply it, or into Matrix Multiply to combine it with another.

nodes.label: Matrix Construction
nodes.description: Builds a matrix from vectors, as its columns or its rows. Columns are how a transform is read: the first two or three are where X, Y and Z go, the last the move. A matrix is one for the whole image, so each vector is read at the image’s centre — for a Constant or an input, simply its value. A vector shorter than the matrix is filled from the identity, so a Vector 2 move becomes the column a 3 × 3 needs, and an unconnected vector is the identity’s own.

nodes.label: Matrix Split
nodes.description: Takes a matrix apart into its columns or its rows, each a vector the same over the whole image: a Vector 2 from a 2 × 2, a Vector 3 from a 3 × 3, a Vector 4 from a 4 × 4. A matrix smaller than the size chosen reads as the identity past its own.

nodes.label: Matrix Multiply
nodes.description: A × B: B applied first, then A — so a move after a turn is the move times the turn. The result is as large as the larger of the two; a smaller matrix meets a larger one padded with the identity.

nodes.label: Matrix Inverse
nodes.description: The matrix that undoes A: A times it is the identity. A matrix that flattens a dimension has none, and gives the identity.

nodes.label: Matrix Transpose
nodes.description: A with its rows and columns swapped. For a pure turn that is its inverse.

nodes.label: Matrix Determinant
nodes.description: How much A scales an area (a 2 × 2, or a 2D transform) or a volume (a 4 × 4): 1 for a turn or a move, the product of the scales otherwise, 0 where it flattens a dimension, and negative where it mirrors. One number, over the whole image.

nodes.label: Matrix Transform
nodes.description: Multiplies every pixel’s vector by a matrix: UVs moved, turned and scaled by a 2D Transform; colors mixed by a 3 × 3; normals or positions turned in 3D. A matrix of size n works on a vector’s first n numbers; a shorter vector is lengthened first, and as a Point it gets a 1 in the last place, so a 3 × 3 moves a UV as well as turning it. A Direction gets a 0 there, so it is turned and scaled but never moved — right for normals and other directions. Numbers past the matrix’s size pass through.

nodes.label: Ease
nodes.description: Reshapes values through a standard easing curve, per channel. Clamp keeps the input inside 0–1, where the curves are defined; the Back and Elastic families deliberately overshoot both ends.
